Goal
Learn the rectangle area formula and how to find missing dimensions.
What is area?
Area measures the surface inside a shape, using unit squares.
Two dimensions
The length and width are perpendicular sides of a rectangle.
Formula
Area equals length times width. Use square units for the answer.
Unit squares
Seven columns of four unit squares make twenty eight squares.
Example one
Seven centimeters times four centimeters gives twenty eight square centimeters.
Missing side
Divide area by the known dimension to find the other dimension.
Example two
Forty eight divided by six gives length eight centimeters.
Check
Eight times six equals forty eight, so the missing side is correct.
Units
Convert both dimensions to matching length units before multiplying.
Perimeter
Perimeter equals twice the sum of length and width.
Perimeter example
If perimeter is thirty and length nine, width six gives area fifty four.
Composite area
Subtract the area of a hole or pond from the whole rectangle.
Garden example
Fourteen times nine minus two times three gives one hundred twenty.
Tiling
Divide floor area by the area of one tile if there is no waste.
Border
An inside border takes its width from both ends of each dimension.
Border example
Eighteen by ten with a two meter border leaves a fourteen by six interior.
Algebra
If length is twice width, area equals two times width squared.
Avoid mistakes
Do not confuse perimeter with area or forget squared units.
